01.r: The Levite and the others are to come and share the stored tithe.
01.n: The verb is singular, agreeing with the Levite, who stands first; the sojourner, fatherless and widow are added after him. The form is a perfect with 'and', which carries on the instruction of the verse before into the future.

02.r: A member of the tribe of Levi, set apart for the sanctuary.
02.n: BDB notes that with the article the word can stand as a collective, for Levites as a class, which suits this law.

03.r: Gives the reason the Levite is included.
03.n: The DRC turns the clause into a description, 'the Levite that hath no other part'.

04.r: Denies that he holds any share of land.
04.n: Gesenius gives the word's base sense as nothing, emptiness, and notes that it often includes the verb 'to be': 'there is not'.

05.r: Marks the Levite as the one who lacks the share.
05.n: Literally 'there is not to him a portion': Hebrew has no verb 'have' and uses 'to' with the owner instead.

06.r: A share of the land, such as the other tribes received.
06.n: The brief's lexicon lists portion, share, and a tract or parcel of land; BDB gives portion, tract, territory.

07.r: Land held by a family and passed down within it.
07.n: Gesenius gives possession, domain, and notes that the word is often used of the territory in the land assigned to each tribe. That is what the Levite lacks.

08.r: Alongside the landholding Israelite addressed by the law.
08.n: The 'you' is singular, as through the whole verse: the law addresses each Israelite as one person.

09.r: Someone living in Israel who was not born into it.
09.n: Gesenius: a sojourner, stranger, foreigner, a person living out of his own country. BDB: a temporary dweller, a newcomer with no inherited rights.

10.r: A child without a father to provide for them.
10.n: Gesenius cites this verse for the word and notes that it is used of a child who has lost only its father, so 'fatherless' is more exact than 'orphan'.

11.r: A woman without a husband to provide for her.

13.n: Hebrew has no 'are' here; the clause is verbless. The brief's lexicon notes that 'gate' can stand for the space inside the gate, and so for the city or town; the Greek translators wrote 'in your cities'.

14.r: They eat from the stored tithe.
14.n: A perfect with 'and', like the verb that opens the verse, so future: 'they shall eat'. YLT renders the perfect form literally, 'they have eaten'.

15.r: They eat until they have had enough.
15.n: BDB: be sated, satisfied, especially with food.

16.r: Gives the purpose of the law.
16.n: The BSB turns the purpose into a promise, 'And the LORD your God will bless you'.

17.r: God's blessing is tied to feeding those without land.
17.n: Gesenius puts 'to bend the knees, to kneel' first among this verb's senses, ahead of 'to bless'.

18.r: The personal name of Israel's God.

19.n: The form is plural but the meaning is singular.

20.r: No part of your work is left out of the blessing.

21.n: Gesenius calls this noun the noun of action of the verb that ends the verse, so 'the work ... that you do' repeats one root.

22.r: The hand that does the work.
22.n: Here the noun is singular, 'your hand'. The DRC and BSB make it plural.

24.r: Whatever you set your hand to.
24.n: Gesenius gives the verb's first sense as to labour, to work about anything, and then to make. The BSB leaves this clause out.

02.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives λευείτης.

04.n: οὐκ ἔστιν, 'there is not', matches the Hebrew idiom exactly.

07.n: κλῆρος means a lot, and so a share assigned by lot.

11.n: The first word, printed κα in our Greek text, is καὶ cut short.

12.n: The Greek uses the article, 'the one in your cities', where the Hebrew has 'who'.

13.n: The Greek says 'in your cities' for 'in your gates'. The first word, printed ἱέν in our Greek text, is evidently ἐν, 'in'.

14.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives φάγω.

15.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives none. The Greek says 'they shall be filled'.

21.n: The Greek has 'in all the works', with no 'of your hand'.

24.n: With ἐὰν before it, 'whatever you do'.
